boundary_rationale: Book onset at the regnal dateline of 1:1 (third year of Jehoiakim). The siege, the removal of the temple vessels, the king's order to Ashpenaz and the naming of the four youths form one setting movement; the unit closes at 1:7 because 1:8 turns to Daniel's own resolve, a new initiative with a new actor-subject.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Dan.1.1 (regnal dateline opening the book)
web:Dan.1.3 (the king speaks to Ashpenaz; the order continues the setting)
web:Dan.1.8 (Daniel's resolve opens the next movement)
strongest_rejected_alternative: Split at 1:2/1:3 so that the siege report (1:1-2) stands alone; rejected because two verses of setting do not form a unit and the 1:3 speech verb is a weak connective that should not open a unit by itself (D4).
strong_or_hebrew_tags_used: oshb:Dan.1.1 בִּשְׁנַ֣ת שָׁל֔וֹשׁ (in the year of ... three: dateline head)
parent_collection: PA (The youths at the Babylonian court)
device_notes: The vayehi of 1:6 introduces the four names inside the selection scene and is read as interior texture, not an onset. 1:4 is a ketiv/qere site (textual variant, disclosed); no boundary is argued from it. The mareh hit at 1:4 is the 'appearance' sense, not a vision.

boundary_rationale: Opens where Daniel sets his heart against the royal food (1:8) and runs through the request, the steward's fear, the ten-day proposal, the test and its result, ending when the steward keeps giving vegetables (1:16). The dietary trial is one episode with a proposal, a trial interval and an outcome.
boundary_evidence_refs: web:Dan.1.8 (Daniel's resolve; new initiative)
web:Dan.1.16 (the steward's continued practice closes the trial)
web:Dan.1.17 (God's gift to the four begins the sequel)
strongest_rejected_alternative: Close at 1:15 and let the vayehi clause of 1:16 open the next unit; rejected because 1:16 reports the consequence of the test and brings in no fresh subject, while the interval clauses in 1:12-15 are texture (D6).
strong_or_hebrew_tags_used: oshb:Dan.1.8 וַיָּ֤שֶׂם דָּנִיֵּאל֙ (and Daniel set: resolve onset)
parent_collection: PA (The youths at the Babylonian court)
device_notes: The ten-day interval recurs at 1:12, 1:14 and 1:15; per D6 these intervals do not set seams. Unmarked stretch, so the seams rest on the text alone.

boundary_rationale: A new subject heads 1:17 (these four youths) with God's gift of learning and Daniel's skill in visions and dreams; 1:18-20 bring them before Nebuchadnezzar at the appointed end and report the examination result. The unit ends before the regnal terminus of 1:21.
boundary_evidence_refs: web:Dan.1.17 (fronted subject: these four youths)
web:Dan.1.18 (the appointed end of the days)
web:Dan.1.21 (terminus notice follows)
strongest_rejected_alternative: Attach 1:21 to this row as its closing verse; rejected because 1:21 is a notice about Daniel's tenure that looks beyond the scene, and a PE follows it, so it is kept as its own summary row (D7).
strong_or_hebrew_tags_used: oshb:Dan.1.17 וְהַיְלָדִ֤ים הָאֵ֨לֶּה֙ אַרְבַּעְתָּ֔ם (and these youths ... four of them)
parent_collection: PA (The youths at the Babylonian court)
device_notes: The hazon of 1:17 anticipates the dream of chapter 2 but is a statement of skill, not a vision report.

boundary_rationale: A one-verse closing notice of Daniel's tenure reaching into the reign of Cyrus. It frames the whole court story and is followed by the parent seam at 1:21/2:1.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Dan.1.21 (PE after this verse, single-witness WLC paragraph mark)
oshb:Dan.2.1 (regnal dateline opening the next parent)
strongest_rejected_alternative: Fold the notice into 1:17-20; rejected because the verse is a tenure statement reaching past the episode, of the kind D7 allows as a one-verse summary_notice row.
strong_or_hebrew_tags_used: oshb:Dan.1.21 וַֽיְהִי֙ דָּֽנִיֵּ֔אל (and Daniel was: tenure notice)
parent_collection: PA (The youths at the Babylonian court)
observed_substrate_signals: year word at 1:21 (regnal terminus, not onset-bearing)
device_notes: The regnal terminus naming Cyrus is left for Fable (device item 1); this row reads it as a closing notice and does not use it as an onset marker.

boundary_rationale: Opens at the regnal dateline of 2:1 (second year of Nebuchadnezzar), with the dream, the summons of the diviners, the king's demand, and the Chaldeans' opening reply. This row covers the 2:4 word-level switch (Hebrew words 1-4, Aramaic words 5 onward), so it ends at 2:4b, holding both 2:4a (Hebrew) and 2:4b (Aramaic); the close after 2:4 rests on the dialogue turn, since 2:5 is the king's answer to that reply.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Dan.1.21 (PE after this verse at the onset seam, single-witness WLC paragraph mark)
oshb:Dan.2.1 (regnal dateline, parent onset)
web:Dan.2.4 (Chaldeans' reply; language switch inside the verse)
web:Dan.2.5 (the king answers: next turn)
strongest_rejected_alternative: Close at 2:3 and begin the following unit at 2:4, so the Aramaic section starts a unit; rejected because the switch falls mid-verse (2:4a Hebrew words 1-4) and the reply belongs to the opening exchange, not the threat that follows.
strong_or_hebrew_tags_used: oshb:Dan.2.1 וּבִשְׁנַ֣ת שְׁתַּ֗יִם (and in the year of two: dateline head)
parent_collection: PB (The king's dream and its interpretation)
observed_substrate_signals: language switch inside 2:4 (Hebrew half words 1-4, Aramaic half words 5-12)
device_notes: Quoted from 2:4b, the Aramaic half, words 5-7: oshb:Dan.2.4 מַלְכָּא֙ לְעָלְמִ֣ין חֱיִ֔י (O king, live forever). 2:4 is also a ketiv/qere site (textual variant, disclosed); the edge at 2:4 is expected to stay weak (region a).

boundary_rationale: The king's threat and promise, the second request, the king's charge of stalling and the Chaldeans' plea that the gods alone could tell form one exchange; 2:12-13 give its outcome, the order to destroy the wise men, reaching Daniel and his companions. A PE follows 2:13.
boundary_evidence_refs: web:Dan.2.5 (the king's answer opens the second turn)
oshb:Dan.2.13 (PE after this verse, single-witness WLC paragraph mark)
web:Dan.2.14 (Daniel's response opens a new movement)
strongest_rejected_alternative: Close at 2:11 and let the decree of 2:12-13 stand as a unit; rejected because because_of_this at 2:12 is a weak connective (D4) and the decree is the direct result of the failed exchange.
strong_or_hebrew_tags_used: oshb:Dan.2.13 וְדָתָ֣א נֶפְקַ֔ת (and the decree went out)
parent_collection: PB (The king's dream and its interpretation)
device_notes: Ketiv/qere sites in span: 2:5, 2:9, 2:10 (textual variants, disclosed; the seams are not argued from them). OSHB editorial note at 2:9 recorded, single witness. The row sits wholly in the Aramaic section.

boundary_rationale: Daniel answers Arioch with discretion, asks why the decree is so urgent, then goes in to the king and asks for time. The short movement ends at the PE after 2:16.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Dan.2.13 (PE after this verse at the onset seam, single-witness WLC paragraph mark)
web:Dan.2.14 (Daniel as new actor)
oshb:Dan.2.16 (PE after this verse, single-witness WLC paragraph mark)
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merge with 2:17-19 as one intervention-and-revelation scene; rejected because the PE after 2:16 and the change of place (to his house, 2:17) both favour a seam there.
parent_collection: PB (The king's dream and its interpretation)
device_notes: The span is Aramaic. The then_aram of 2:14 comes with a change of actor; it is not read as an onset by itself.

boundary_rationale: Daniel goes home, tells his companions, and asks them to seek mercy from the God of heaven; the secret is shown to him in a night vision and he blesses God. The praise that follows is a separate speech act.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Dan.2.16 (PE after this verse at the onset seam, single-witness WLC paragraph mark)
web:Dan.2.17 (Daniel goes home: change of place)
web:Dan.2.19 (secret revealed; Daniel blesses)
web:Dan.2.20 (the praise itself begins)
strongest_rejected_alternative: Run 2:17-2:23 as one row closing on the doxology (D1); rejected in favour of a hymn row because 2:20-23 has its own speaker formula and a self-contained praise form.
parent_collection: PB (The king's dream and its interpretation)
device_notes: Aramaic narrative. The night vision of 2:19 is reported in one clause; its content is told later, at 2:31-35.

boundary_rationale: Daniel's praise blesses God's name, the one who changes times, gives wisdom and reveals deep things; it ends with thanks to the God of his fathers for making the king's matter known. The hymn is a closed speech act.
boundary_evidence_refs: web:Dan.2.20 (blessing formula opening the praise)
web:Dan.2.23 (thanks and praise closing it)
web:Dan.2.24 (Daniel goes to Arioch: action resumes)

boundary_rationale: Daniel stops the executions through Arioch, is brought before the king, is asked whether he can tell the dream, and answers that no wise man can but a God in heaven reveals secrets; the preamble ends at 2:30 before the dream report begins.
boundary_evidence_refs: oshb:Dan.2.24 (SAMEKH after this verse, single-witness WLC paragraph mark)
oshb:Dan.2.28 (PE after this verse, single-witness WLC paragraph mark)
web:Dan.2.31 (the report of what the king saw begins)

device_notes: Aramaic dialogue; 2:26 is a ketiv/qere site (textual variant, disclosed). The PE after 2:28 falls inside Daniel's preamble and is held as interior.

boundary_rationale: Daniel recounts the dream: the great image, its metals, the stone cut without hands, the image shattered and the stone grown to a mountain. The report and its interpretation part at 2:35/2:36 and nowhere else inside 2:31-45 (guard d).
boundary_evidence_refs: web:Dan.2.31 (you saw, and behold: report onset)
web:Dan.2.34 (you saw until: second step)
web:Dan.2.36 (this is the dream: turn to interpretation)
strongest_rejected_alternative: Keep report and interpretation in one row 2:31-45 as one speech by Daniel; rejected because 2:36 explicitly closes the dream and announces the interpretation, the seam that guard (d) permits (region b).

parent_collection: PB (The king's dream and its interpretation)
device_notes: Aramaic report. Per D5 the i_was_seeing formula at 2:34 steps the scene inside the report and does not open a unit. 2:33 is a ketiv/qere site (textual variant, disclosed).

boundary_rationale: Single speech act, stated: 2:36-45 is one interpretation speech by Daniel (ten verses), from 'this is the dream' through the four kingdoms and the everlasting kingdom to 'the dream is certain', so it exceeds nine verses by design. The PE after 2:45 closes it.

parent_collection: PB (The king's dream and its interpretation)
device_notes: The interpretation is in Aramaic. Ketiv/qere sites in span: 2:38, 2:39, 2:40, 2:41, 2:42, 2:43 (textual variants, disclosed). OSHB editorial notes at 2:37, 2:38, 2:39 and 2:41 recorded, single witness; no seam is argued from them.

boundary_rationale: The king falls prostrate, confesses Daniel's God, and promotes Daniel and, at his request, his three companions; the chapter ends with Daniel in the king's gate. The next verse opens a new episode with the golden image.
